ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Read the figure “precipitation amounts on the south and north slopes of a certain mountain”: <image1> According to the distribution characteristics of precipitation on the south and north slopes in the figure, determine which mountain range this place most likely belongs to.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a mountain profile graph showing changes in precipitation amount and elevation. The legend shows that the dashed line represents “elevation” and the solid line represents “rainfall.” The left vertical axis is precipitation amount, with the unit in millimeters, and the values are roughly between 90—170 millimeters; the right vertical axis is elevation, with the unit in meters, and the highest is close to 1800 meters. The “wind direction” arrow above the figure points to the right, indicating that the airflow moves from left to right. The solid-line precipitation amount is relatively high on the windward side, reaches a relatively high value before approaching the high part of the mountain, then drops obviously on the other side after crossing the mountain and continues to decrease. The overall precipitation amount values are not high, showing the characteristics of mountain precipitation in an inland arid region. Then reason: This question asks to determine the mountain range according to the distribution of precipitation on the south and north slopes. The feature shown in the figure is that one side of the mountain is affected by moist airflow and has more precipitation, while the other side is in the leeward rain-shadow area and has obviously less precipitation; moreover, the overall precipitation is relatively low, conforming to the precipitation pattern of mountains in China’s northwestern inland region. The northern slope of China’s Tianshan Mountains is affected by the westerlies and water vapor from the Atlantic Ocean and Arctic Ocean directions, so precipitation is relatively more; the southern slope faces the Tarim Basin and, affected by the rain-shadow effect, has a drier climate and less precipitation. Therefore, this mountain is most likely the Tianshan Mountains.

raw_record.question_text:
Read the figure “precipitation amounts on the south and north slopes of a certain mountain”:

<image1>

According to the distribution characteristics of precipitation on the south and north slopes in the figure, determine which mountain range this place most likely belongs to.

method.method_draft: First describe the plotted features: identify the solid line as precipitation, the dashed line as altitude, and note the left-to-right wind direction. Observe that precipitation is concentrated on the windward/one side of the mountain and declines markedly on the opposite slope, with generally low values typical of an arid inland region. Then use the text requirement—judge the mountain from north-south slope precipitation distribution—and match this pattern to a Chinese mountain range whose north slope is wetter and south slope drier due to westerlies and rain shadow. Conclude that the mountain is the Tianshan Mountains.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中是一幅山地剖面降水量与海拔高度变化图。图例显示，虚线表示“高度”，实线表示“雨量”。左侧纵轴为降水量，单位为毫米，数值大致在90—170毫米之间；右侧纵轴为海拔高度，单位为米，最高接近1800米。图上方“风向”箭头指向右侧，说明气流由左向右运动。实线降水量在迎风一侧相对较高，接近山体高处前达到较高值，越过山地后在另一侧明显下降，并继续降低，整体降水量数值不高，表现出内陆干旱区山地降水的特征。

再推理：该题要求根据南北坡降水量分布判断山脉。图示特征是山地一侧受湿润气流影响降水较多，另一侧处于背风雨影区，降水明显偏少；并且整体降水偏少，符合我国西北内陆山地的降水格局。我国天山山脉北坡受西风带及来自大西洋、北冰洋方向水汽影响，降水相对较多；南坡面向塔里木盆地，受雨影效应影响，气候更干旱，降水较少。因此该山地最可能是天山山脉。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Uses the image’s windward/leeward precipitation asymmetry and low absolute precipitation range to match a known Chinese mountain climate pattern; this is the direct and most robust route, so only one genuinely distinct method is provided.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the graph as a mountain cross-section: the dashed line is altitude, peaking near the center; the solid line is precipitation. The wind-direction arrow points from left to right. Precipitation is higher on the left/windward side, with a maximum around the upper windward slope, then drops sharply on the right/leeward side and decreases toward about 90 mm.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt’s instruction that the key evidence is the distribution of precipitation on the north and south slopes of an unnamed mountain, and that the answer should be a mountain range name.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply orographic precipitation knowledge: windward slopes receive more precipitation, leeward slopes are drier. Among major Chinese mountains, the Tianshan Mountains are in inland Xinjiang, affected by westerly moisture; the north/windward slope is wetter while the south/leeward side toward the Tarim Basin is much drier, and overall precipitation is relatively low, matching the graph.
